newsitem.title: EGYPT: Five dead in shootout in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Five dead in shootout in south Egypt.

text.p: Four suspected Moslem militants and a farmer died in southern Egypt during a shootout between police and members of the country's largest armed Islamist group, security sources said on Monday.

They said the incident took place on Sunday while police were combing fields in the southern province of Beni Sueif in search for members of al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) wanted for a number of violent crimes.
Farmer Mohammed Hassan Sayyed, 32, who was in his fields at the time of the shootout, was caught in the crossfire and died later in hospital, the sources said.
An Interior Ministry statement said only two Gama'a members were killed when police returned their fire during the manhunt.

The statement said the two militants belonged to the military wing of the Gama'a and had taken part in various attacks, including murder and armed robbery of jewellry stores and banks in southern Egypt.

The Gama'a in 1992 launched a bloody campaign to overthrow the Egyptian government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people, mainly police and militants, have been killed in political violence since.
